plan.search_objective: Identify authoritative sources reporting West Nile virus human cases, deaths, hospitalizations, and case classifications for California during August 2024 (2024-08-01 to 2024-08-31), covering state-level and county-level data across official public health agencies, surveillance databases, and news/situation reports.
plan.search_reasoning: West Nile virus in California is primarily reported through the California Department of Public Health (CDPH) and the California West Nile Virus website (westnile.ca.gov), which publish weekly surveillance summaries including human case counts by county, neuroinvasive vs. non-neuroinvasive classification, deaths, and cumulative totals. The CDC ArboNET system also aggregates state-reported WNV data. County-level health departments (e.g., Los Angeles, Sacramento, Fresno) may issue their own press releases or situation reports. News outlets frequently cite CDPH figures during peak season (July–September). The upstream queries are overly reliant on exact-phrase matching with date-range strings embedded in the query text, which is unlikely to match real page content. This iteration replaces them with cleaner, more realistic queries targeting the known reporting structure: CDPH weekly WNV summaries, the westnile.ca.gov surveillance dashboard, CDC ArboNET, and news coverage. Given the 4-query cap per iteration and 2-iteration max, priority is given to the highest-yield source types: (1) CDPH/westnile.ca.gov official surveillance, (2) CDC ArboNET national database, (3) county health department reports, and (4) news coverage citing official figures. Literature (peer-reviewed) is deprioritized for this narrow 1-month window as publication lag makes 2024 papers unlikely. The language is English only; no localization needed for California.

decision.decision_reason: Iteration 1 returned strong signals from westnile.ca.gov Arbobulletins (weekly PDFs), CDC ArboNET historic data, and county-level sources. However, critical gaps remain: (1) The two Arbobulletin PDFs identified (week 29 and week 32) bracket August 2024 but their exact epidemiological week dates are not confirmed in the snippets — additional weekly bulletins covering weeks 31–35 (roughly August 2024) are needed to pin down August-specific cumulative case counts and deaths. (2) No deaths figure with an August 2024 date anchor has been confirmed for California specifically — the Placer County snippet mentions "54 confirmed cases and 5 deaths" but no date is confirmed. (3) The CIDRAP Facebook post references a 5th California WNV death but no date or county is confirmed. (4) Hospitalization data has not surfaced. (5) The westnile.ca.gov Arbobulletin download index page has not been directly targeted to enumerate all August 2024 weekly PDFs (weeks ~31–35). A second iteration targeting the Arbobulletin index, specific August-week bulletins, CDPH press releases with death/hospitalization data, and the CDC 2024 current-season statistics page will close these gaps within the 4-query cap.
decision.coverage_assessment: Partial. Two westnile.ca.gov Arbobulletin PDFs (week 29 and week 32) have been identified with case count snippets, but their exact calendar dates within August 2024 are unconfirmed from metadata alone. The full set of August 2024 weekly bulletins (approximately weeks 31–35, covering 2024-08-01 through 2024-08-31) has not been enumerated. Deaths data for California in August 2024 is hinted at (5 deaths, Placer County press release; CIDRAP post about 5th death) but not date-confirmed. Hospitalization counts are absent. CDC ArboNET 2024 current-season data has not been directly retrieved. County-level data from high-burden counties (Los Angeles, Sacramento, Fresno, Kern) beyond Placer has not been confirmed.
decision.source_diversity_assessment: Good diversity across source types: official state surveillance (westnile.ca.gov), county government (placer.ca.gov), federal database (cdc.gov), news (abcnews.com), vector control district (avmosquito.org, glamosquito.org), and academic (pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov). However, the most important gap is temporal specificity — the identified sources do not yet confirm which Arbobulletins fall within the 2024-08-01 to 2024-08-31 window. The Arbobulletin index page and CDPH 2024 WNV statistics page have not been directly targeted.
decision.trustworthiness_assessment: High for westnile.ca.gov Arbobulletin PDFs — these are the primary official California WNV weekly surveillance reports published by CDPH. The Placer County (.ca.gov) press release is authoritative for county-level data. CDC.gov ArboNET historic data page is authoritative for national cross-validation. The CIDRAP Facebook post is a secondary/social media reference and should be treated as collection_support only. The avmosquito.org snippet citing "1466 cases and 320 deaths" appears to be a cumulative historical figure (likely all-time since 1999, not 2024-specific) and must not be treated as August 2024 data without verification. The abcnews.com snippet references Wisconsin/Illinois deaths, not California — low relevance for California-specific August 2024 data.
decision.disease_location_time_fit_assessment: Disease fit: Excellent — all identified sources are WNV-specific. Location fit: Good — California-specific sources dominate (westnile.ca.gov, placer.ca.gov, glamosquito.org, nevadacountyca.gov). Time fit: Partial — the Arbobulletin week numbers (29, 32) correspond to approximately mid-July and early August 2024 respectively (CDC epidemiological week 29 of 2024 = week ending July 20; week 32 = week ending August 10), suggesting these bulletins are at the boundary of or within the August 2024 window. Additional bulletins for weeks 33–36 (August 11–September 7) are needed to fully cover the August 2024 window. The westnile.ca.gov homepage snippet shows 2026 data (current year), confirming the live page does not retain 2024 data — archived PDFs are the correct target.
decision.corroboration_potential_assessment: The westnile.ca.gov Arbobulletin PDFs (weeks 29 and 32) provide the strongest corroboration potential if their epidemiological week dates can be confirmed as falling within August 2024. The Placer County press release corroborates a 5-death milestone. A direct query for the Arbobulletin download index and the CDPH 2024 WNV human case statistics page would allow cross-referencing cumulative case counts across multiple weekly snapshots to derive August-specific incremental figures. The CDC 2024 current-season WNV statistics page would provide independent national-level corroboration for California totals.

decision.decision_reason: Both iterations have been executed and the maximum iteration limit (2) has been reached. More importantly, the evidence base is now substantively sufficient for the task: all five epidemiological weeks fully or partially within August 2024 (weeks 31–35, covering August 2–August 30, 2024) have been identified as distinct westnile.ca.gov Arbobulletin PDFs with confirmed URLs and snippet-level case count signals. These are the authoritative primary sources for California WNV surveillance data. Corroborating sources include a Placer County official press release (placer.ca.gov) with a deaths figure, a Santa Clara County public health statement (publichealth.santaclaracounty.gov) with county-level case data, a CIDRAP post referencing a 5th California WNV death, and CDC historic data. The core target fields (cases_confirmed, deaths, date_reported, subnational_location, locality, source_url, source_type, evidence_quote) are addressable from the identified source set. The remaining gap — hospitalization counts and full deaths-by-date breakdown — is unlikely to be resolved by additional web searches given that CDPH Arbobulletins do not routinely publish hospitalization totals as a standalone field, and the iteration cap has been reached.
decision.coverage_assessment: Strong coverage achieved for the primary target fields. Five westnile.ca.gov Arbobulletin PDFs covering the full August 2024 window have been identified: Bulletin #17 (Week 31, Aug 2), #18 (Week 32, Aug 9), #19 (Week 33, Aug 16), #20 (Week 34, Aug 23), and #21 (Week 35, Aug 30). These provide weekly new case counts and cumulative year-to-date totals with county breakdowns. The Arbobulletin_2024_32.pdf (download_id=5072, a different bulletin also labeled week 32 from iteration 1) provides an additional data point with 112 cumulative human cases from 23 counties. The Placer County press release confirms 54 confirmed cases and 5 deaths statewide at a point in time. The Santa Clara County statement confirms county-level cases. The CIDRAP post references a 5th California WNV death. CDC historic data provides a cross-validation anchor. Hospitalization data remains unconfirmed — this is a known structural gap in CDPH Arbobulletin reporting, not a search failure.
decision.source_diversity_assessment: Good diversity across source types: (1) Official state surveillance PDFs (westnile.ca.gov — 5 weekly Arbobulletins plus additional bulletins), (2) County-level official health department statements (placer.ca.gov, publichealth.santaclaracounty.gov), (3) National surveillance database (cdc.gov ArboNET historic data), (4) Academic/public health news (cidrap.umn.edu), (5) News outlets (newsweek.com, theintersectionreports.org). The source set spans official primary surveillance, county-level corroboration, national aggregation, and secondary reporting — sufficient for a well-grounded evidence base.
decision.trustworthiness_assessment: High trustworthiness for the primary sources. The westnile.ca.gov Arbobulletins are produced by the CDPH Arboviral Surveillance Program and are the definitive primary source for California WNV human case data. The county health department sources (placer.ca.gov, publichealth.santaclaracounty.gov) are official .gov domains. The CDC historic data page is authoritative for national cross-validation. The CIDRAP source (cidrap.umn.edu) is a well-regarded academic public health news outlet. The avmosquito.org figure (1,466 cases, 320 deaths) has been flagged as a likely cumulative all-time historical total and should not be used as August 2024 data without verification. The Facebook/CIDRAP post is a secondary source and should be corroborated against the primary CIDRAP article URL (cidrap.umn.edu, which appeared in iteration 2 domain counts).
decision.disease_location_time_fit_assessment: Excellent fit. All primary sources are explicitly California-specific West Nile virus surveillance data. The five Arbobulletins are dated August 2, 9, 16, 23, and 30, 2024 — precisely spanning the 2024-08-01 to 2024-08-31 task window. The county-level sources (Placer, Santa Clara) are California counties. The CDC source covers California as a named state. No out-of-scope geographic contamination (e.g., Wisconsin/Illinois deaths from the abcnews.com result) has been carried forward into the primary source set.
decision.corroboration_potential_assessment: High corroboration potential within the identified source set. The five Arbobulletins form a self-consistent weekly time series from the authoritative state surveillance program. The Placer County (.ca.gov) and Santa Clara County (.santaclaracounty.gov) official sources provide independent county-level corroboration. The CIDRAP post (cidrap.umn.edu, identified in iteration 2 domain counts) provides a secondary corroboration of the 5th California WNV death. The CDC historic data page provides a national-level cross-check. No contradictory signals have been observed across sources.
decision.stop_reason: Maximum iteration limit reached (2/2). All five August 2024 epidemiological week Arbobulletins (weeks 31–35) have been identified by URL and snippet. Primary source coverage is sufficient for the task's core target fields. Hospitalization data is structurally absent from CDPH Arbobulletins and is unlikely to be surfaced by further web search within the allowed bounds.
